To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel serrawetttin W1 producing strain was isolated, that the respective biosurfactant gene was cloned into E. coli and that the heterologously produced biosurfactant is chemically very similar to the native one.
the biosurfactant Serrawettin W-1 was successfully produced in Escherichiacoli BL21 Gold using the nonribosomal peptide gene swrW of Serratia. marcescencs DSM 12481.

Serratia marcessens strain DSM1248 is a novel serrawetthin W1 producing strain, that the swrW gene was cloned and expressed for the first time in Escherichiac coli, and that the biosynthetic machinery of Serratia and Escherichia is similar.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of the biosurfactant Serrawettin W 1 by Escherichia colli and its application in the field of bioremediation.
the heterologous production and characterization of the biosurfactant Serrawettin W-1 in Eschericchia coli.
the development of a new production platform for the biosurfactant Serrawettin W.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heterologous expression of the serrawettin gene in Escherichium coli is possible and that this method is a good starting point to produce this biotechnologically interesting biosurfactant.
the production of the biosurfactant Serrawettin W-1 in E. coli BL21 Gold is feasible and that the biosynthetic gene swrW is a good target for genetic manipulation.
heterologous expression of swrW in E. coli resulted in the production of the lipodepsipeptide serrawettin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonribosomal peptide biosynthesis is not only restricted to bacteria, fungi and plants but also to E. coli.
we could show that the non-ionic biosufactant serrawettins can be heterologously produced in E. coli, which opens the possibility for the large-scale production of this biologically active compound.
a novel biosurfactant producer Serratia marcsens DSM 12481 and the respective non-ribosomal peptide synthase gene swr W were identified.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to express a biosynthetic gene cluster from a Gram-negative soil bacterium in a Gram-positive bacterium, E. coli.
the biosynthesis of serrawettin in Escherichiacoli was successful and the heterologously produced serrawettins showed similar properties as the natural product.
the heterologous expression of the serrawettin biosynthesis genes in E. coli is a promising approach to increase the production of serrawettin.
